transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-02-12
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 70 mins
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jon (Redwood SE), Sara (Acme Head of ML), Tom (Acme Platform), Priya (Acme Product)

Summary:
Quick scoping to align on POC timeline & milestones: kickoff, access setup, mid-point review, exec readout. Agree on success criteria (latency, throughput, cost, quality), workload sizing and benchmark plan. Discuss security/VPC needs and next steps.

Topics covered:
- POC timeline and milestones
- Access and infra prerequisites (VPC, IAM, dataset)
- Workload sizing: tokens/sec, concurrency, seq len distribution
- Benchmark types: synthetic, replay, end-to-end latency and cost modeling
- Success criteria and go/no-go gates
- Risks and mitigations (data residency, SOC2, KMS)

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): okay everyone, thanks for joining, we'll run about an hour, agenda is scoping the POC timeline and milestones. quick intros?
[00:12] Sara (Acme): hi, Sara here, head of ML, i'll own success criteria and coordinate with product
[00:18] Tom (Acme): Tom, platform eng, i'll handle infra bits, vpc/iam etc
[00:22] Priya (Acme): Priya, product, i'll share user flows and intent lists
[00:27] Jon (Redwood SE): Jon from SE, i'll own benchmarks and perf validation

[01:05] Maya: high level POC we usually do 4 weeks, kickoff -> access setup -> run baselines -> midpoint review -> run improvements -> exec readout. think of it as 2 cycles: initial baseline (weeks 1-2) and optimization (weeks 3-4). does that map to your timelines?
[01:30] Sara: we were hoping 3-4 weeks, must be done before end of march for exec. 4 weeks is fine as long as we have a clear mid-point review to show progress.
[01:44] Priya: important the exec readout shows clear metrics vs current system, esp latency and cost per 1k queries

[03:10] Jon: For workload sizing can you give rough traffic? tokens per request, concurrency, percent of long seqs?
[03:22] Sara: current baseline: 50 qps burst, steady around 10 qps. avg tokens in prompt+response ~ 400 tokens, 95th perc length is 1200 both directions. monthly volume roughly 3M queries. goal is to test both read path (fast generation for responses) and a reranking/embedding path for search.
[03:50] Tom: also we'd like to test concurrency up to 100 for peak sim; we can provide replay logs for a sample week.

[05:00] Jon: perfect. Our benchmark plan: (a) synthetic microbenchmarks to validate latency/throughput on your target instance types, (b) replay-based end-to-end benchmarks using your logs to measure real latency distribution and token costs, (c) quality checks on top intents — compare outputs vs your golden set. we'll do baseline using our hosted models and then try dedicated instance if you want to validate reserved capacity.
[05:35] Sara: quality thresholds: we want less than 5% regression on our rubric and median latency under 300ms for simple prompts, p95 under 1.5s. cost target is at least 25% improvement vs our current managed provider.
[05:50] Maya: sounds good. we'll put those as success criteria: quality <=5% regression, median latency <300ms, p95 <1.5s for primary flows, cost per 1k down by 25%. any additional SLAs?
[06:05] Priya: reliability and consistent tail behavior matter — noisy p95 spikes would be bad.

[08:10] Tom: security questions — we need SOC2, SSO/SAML, audit logs, KMS for keys, and VPC peering or private link. can you support on-prem or VPC deployment for the POC?
[08:35] Maya: yes. for most enterprise POCs we offer private deployment (VPC) or hosted with VPC peering. we have SOC2 reports and security pack, we can share the docs. for KMS we support customer-managed keys in dedicated/private.
[09:00] Tom: good — i'll need network IPs, egress rules, and an IAM role, we'll provide a test S3 bucket for sample data access.

[11:20] Jon: timeline detail: Week 0 kickoff + access setup (VPC, IAM, S3). Week 1 run synthetic microbenchmarks and get baseline. Week 2 run replay benchmarks + quality eval. Mid-point review end of week 2 with results and proposed optimization plan. Week 3-4 apply optimizations (quantization, batching, routing) and re-run benchmarks. Executive readout week 4 with a one-pager and slide deck.
[11:55] Sara: mid-point review should include representative dashboards: latency histograms, cost per token, accuracy on golden set, and open issues.
[12:10] Jon: we'll provide a dashboard snapshot and the raw CSVs. also propose a short canary on dedicated mode if you want to validate configuration.

[14:40] Priya: what about dataset privacy? our logs contain PII, will Redwood handle redaction or do we need to scrub?
[14:55] Maya: good question — we recommend scrubbing before upload; we can also run inside your VPC/private deployment to keep logs in your environment. if you provide a scrubbed sample we can proceed faster.

[16:30] Sara: benchmarks — what metrics will you produce?
[16:40] Jon: latency median/p95/p99, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, throughput at target concurrency, and quality deltas against golden set. we'll also estimate production unit economics using your traffic profile.

[20:00] Tom: for infra, i'll open a ticket to provision an IAM role and S3 link. expect that by Monday.
[20:10] Maya: great. on our side, we'll send the POC engagement doc and pricing options. Also Redwood SE will share the replay harness and the perf checklist.

[22:30] Priya: anything about rollback or fallback? if we go dedicated and see regressions, we need safe fallback to hosted or previous provider.
[22:45] Jon: we support routing policies and automatic fallback to a stable model/region; for the POC we can configure a policy to avoid risk.

[25:00] Sara: success gating — if after week 4 we don't hit the latency or cost gates, is there an option to extend POC with an engineering add-on?
[25:12] Maya: yes, we can propose an optimization engagement; we'll outline that in pricing.

[30:00] (cross talk / side note about integration complexity)

[41:00] Maya: recap: action items — Redwood to send docs, SE to run baseline, Acme to provide access and dataset, schedule kickoff for next Tue. mid-point review end of week 2; exec readout week 4.
[41:25] Tom: confirm i'll share VPC/IAM by Mon and sample logs by Wed.
[41:40] Sara: i'll finalize success criteria doc and invite stakeholders for exec readout.

[42:05] Maya: any other blockers?
[42:12] Priya: none from product side.
[42:20] Jon: i'll start preparing the replay harness, will ask for a quick sync after you drop the logs.

[43:00] Maya: thanks everyone, i'll send meeting notes and next steps.
[43:05] Sara: thanks all, bye.

End of transcript.
